clue.text: Peculiar dictionary is unreliable — head for Chambers

indicators.note: something unreliable cannot be trusted to stay as it is, so the letters before it are rearranged
the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A grumble that a dictionary is untrustworthy, recommending the solver turn to Chambers instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unreliable' rearranges DICTIONARY IS into IDIOSYNCRATI; 'head for' supplies the C of Chambers at the end. Chambers is the dictionary crossword setters favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something idiosyncratic is peculiar to one person, odd and individual in its character.

clue.text: Irritable idler wandering around ruined temple

indicators.note: the first scrambled group goes around the outside of the second, holding it within
wandering means moving about aimlessly, so the letters of idler are jumbled
something ruined is broken up, so the letters of temple are rearranged

explanation.surface: An irritable loafer roams about a temple in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: The two anagrams are kept apart: 'around' puts the scrambled temple inside the scrambled idler, not one pool of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-tempered describes someone grumpy and quick to anger, a direct synonym of irritable.

clue.text: Rudimentary measure of grain not complete

parts.note: an inch is a measure of length

indicators.note: a word not complete lacks its final letter, so the last one is dropped

parts.note: oaten means made of oats, a grain

explanation.surface: A unit for measuring grain that is only partly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of grain' looks like part of the measure phrase, but it is the adjective for oats, which 'not complete' shortens.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means only just begun and not fully formed, so basic or rudimentary.

clue.text: Men in foul conditions in newspaper article

indicators.note: the first 'in' says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a sty is a filthy place, as in a pigsty
OR, other ranks, is the military term for enlisted men

explanation.surface: Men living in squalor, as reported in a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A story is a piece of news reporting, the item a journalist files.

clue.text: Navy getting new cut in fuel, greater than any previous?

indicators.note: says the pieces before it go inside the fuel word

parts.note: oil is a fuel
to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: The Navy reduces its fuel spending to an unprecedented degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a loose definition: something without equal surpasses all before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil means having no equal, matchless, unsurpassed by anything that has gone before.

clue.text: Official replacing top of substantial shelter

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is swapped out for the official

parts.note: huge means very large or substantial
a ref, referee, is a sports official

explanation.surface: A referee takes the place of the leader of a large shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing top of' swaps the H of HUGE for REF.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge is a place of safety offering protection, which is a shelter.

clue.text: Three stripped — feature of Glastonbury?

indicators.note: stripped means its outer layer is removed, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a cross-reference to the answer at 3 down, which is story

explanation.surface: A group of three undressed at the Glastonbury festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three' is not a number but the answer to 3 down; 'stripped' removes its outside letters, leaving TOR. Glastonbury, in Somerset, England, is famous for its hill, Glastonbury Tor, as well as its music festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hill, and Glastonbury Tor is the town's best-known landmark.

clue.text: Disadvantage to hear a song

definitions.meaning: a ... is a hidden drawback, as in 'what's the ...?'
to ... something said is to hear it
a round, a song sung by voices entering in turn

explanation.surface: A downside of listening to a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Catch carries all three senses: a snag, the act of hearing, and a type of round sung in canon.

clue.text: Take to court, involving one embracing mostly violent activity

indicators.note: the court word wraps around, involving, the other piece

parts.note: to try someone is to put them on trial in court

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a hugger is one who embraces

explanation.surface: Suing someone who hugged you, because it was mostly violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take to court' suggests SUE, but the trial sense is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuggery is the brutal behaviour of thugs, aggressive violence.

clue.text: Prince with severe expression covering front of curious old coin

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V

indicators.note: the frown wraps around the next letter, covering it

parts.note: a frown is a stern look

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A stern-faced prince examining an odd old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-crown was a pre-decimal British coin worth two shillings and sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: The half-crown was a British coin withdrawn in 1970, so an old piece of money.

clue.text: Hand round recipe that's original

indicators.note: the hand word goes round the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, seen on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Passing a recipe round that's a novel one.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of something is the original, the one that came before all others.

clue.text: King, for one, blocking distasteful pope

indicators.note: the inserted letters block the middle of the other word

parts.note: gory means bloody and so distasteful
R is for rex, Latin for king
EG, for example, means 'for one'

explanation.surface: A king stands in the way of an unpleasant pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregory is the name of sixteen popes, including Gregory the Great.

clue.text: Article to say rather too much about one's pain

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the talk word goes about the numeral, surrounding it

parts.note: to gush is to talk effusively, saying too much
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: An essay that overstates someone's suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests writing, but here it is just AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering, so pain.

clue.text: One million continue accepting one saint's beliefs

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the continue phrase takes in, accepts, the numeral

parts.note: to press on is to continue
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: One in a million persists in holding a saint's convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressions are the views or opinions one forms, hence beliefs.

clue.text: Person overseas, seeing abdication of Queen, is to say more

indicators.note: when a queen abdicates she departs, so her letter leaves the word

parts.note: an expatriate lives abroad
R is for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An expat watching the Queen give up the throne has more to say about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abdication of' takes R out of EXPATRIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length on a subject, elaborating further.

clue.text: Excellent to beset castle I supplied with soldiers, having stronger reason

indicators.note: to beset is to surround, so the excellent letters go round the others

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: the I is supplied with the soldiers, which follow it

parts.note: a fort is a castle
OR, other ranks, are soldiers below officer level

explanation.surface: A splendid assault on a castle I had manned with troops.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORTIORI is Latin for 'from the stronger argument', used of a conclusion that follows even more surely.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortiori is used when one conclusion holds with stronger reason than one already accepted.

clue.text: Father engaging in kinky sex? I don't want that in my inbox

definitions.text: I don't want that in my inbox

indicators.note: the father word engages in, enters, the sex abbreviation

parts.note: S and M, sadomasochism, is kinky sex
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father involved in something kinky, and the recipient does not want to receive the email about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unsolicited junk email, unwelcome in anyone's inbox.

clue.text: Wine, one inspiring line about tiger?

indicators.note: the muse and line go about the cat

parts.note: a muse inspires artists
a tiger is an example of a big cat, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A wine that inspired a poem about a tiger.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscatel is a sweet wine made from muscat grapes.

clue.text: Lines in sonnet? There's support for us in folio note

definitions.note: a number answers how many lines are in a sonnet

indicators.note: the support phrase goes in between the folio and note letters

parts.note: our means belonging to us, for us
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A supportive remark found in a note in a folio volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a poem of fourteen lines, so the number counts them.

clue.text: City prominent in history or knowledge

indicators.note: the answer stands out within the run of words, its letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A city that features in history and knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: York is a historic cathedral city in northern England.

clue.text: People observing toilet in New York city not unknown

indicators.note: the toilet word goes in the trimmed city
not having the letter, so it is taken away

parts.note: Yonkers is a city in New York State
Y is an algebraic unknown
loo is a British word for toilet

explanation.surface: People watching a toilet in a New York city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' drops Y from YONKERS to leave ONKERS, which takes LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Onlookers are spectators, people who watch without taking part.

clue.text: Being aboard very large boat

indicators.note: the being word goes aboard, inside, the two letters

parts.note: esse is Latin for being, used in English philosophy

explanation.surface: Someone is aboard a very big boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is a ship or boat, any craft that carries people on water.

clue.text: To say more in French is, after a touch of Spanish, most regrettable

indicators.note: the other pieces come after the Spanish letter
a touch is just a little, the first letter

parts.note: to add is to say more
est is the French for is

explanation.surface: Saying more in French, after a little Spanish, is a great shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddest is the superlative of sad, so most regrettable or unfortunate.

clue.text: Designation of fighter plane brought in to fly until now

indicators.note: the plane letter is brought into the flying word

parts.note: to soar is to fly high
F is the US designation for fighter aircraft, as in F-16

explanation.surface: A fighter plane's code is brought in to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: So far means up to the present time, until now.

clue.text: Cheers after Pole is getting job in cafe

definitions.note: loosely, the person doing that job

indicators.note: the thanks word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a bar is a pole or rod
ta is British slang for thanks, cheers

explanation.surface: A Pole, after thanks, is getting work in a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it is a rod, BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista makes and serves coffee in a coffee shop, the person in that post.

clue.text: Beer half-heartedly provided for nipper

indicators.note: one of the two middle letters, half the heart, is removed

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer

explanation.surface: Beer being given out reluctantly to a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' looks like a child, but it is one that nips.
explanation.definitionFit: A biter is one that bites, and to nip is to bite.

clue.text: Fellow shows agitation, losing women's cutlery

indicators.note: losing means letting go of the letter, which is dropped

parts.note: works, as a face works with emotion, shows agitation
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A man gets agitated when he loses the women's cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: Forks are eating implements, part of a set of cutlery.

clue.text: Some theatre clearly is place for play

indicators.note: some of the words, a portion, contains the answer

explanation.surface: Part of the theatre is plainly a place to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place for play' suggests a stage, but it is the playground.
explanation.definitionFit: A rec is short for recreation ground, a British public park for games.

clue.text: To win only subsequently leads to optimism seen in an individual

indicators.note: the pieces go in the individual word

parts.note: one is a single individual
then means subsequently

indicators.note: the leads are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Winning only later brings optimism to a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet on the nose is a racing wager that a horse wins outright, not just places.

clue.text: Awkward customers restrict canal, milling around

indicators.note: milling around means moving about randomly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Awkward people block a canal by milling about.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalcitrants are stubborn people who resist authority, difficult characters.
